title: Day 608 — CNTE National Strike: Megamarch from Ángel de la Independencia Shuts Down Mexico City; 29 States Affected
detail: On June 1, 2026 (Day 608), the CNTE's (Coordinadora Nacional de Trabajadores de la Educación) announced national work stoppage began, with teachers from 29 states conducting a simultaneous strike and a megamarch in Mexico City. Departing from the Ángel de la Independencia on Paseo de la Reforma at approximately 9:00 AM, tens of thousands of teachers marched toward the Zócalo and Centro Histórico. El Financiero's live coverage reported major street closures throughout the morning: Paseo de la Reforma, Av. Juárez, Eje Central, 5 de Mayo, Av. Madero, and 16 de Septiembre. The Zócalo main plaza was partially inaccessible due to FIFA World Cup 2026 Fan Fest infrastructure already installed ahead of the June 11 Mexico vs. South Africa inaugural match. The CNTE's core demands remained unchanged: (1) abrogation of the 2007 ISSSTE pension law; (2) 100% salary increase; (3) elimination of the teacher career evaluation/dismissal system; (4) direct hiring of teachers without evaluation. Three rounds of SEGOB-SEP-ISSSTE dialogue (culminating in the May 29 seven-hour session) had yielded no movement on core demands, triggering the June 1 escalation. Section leaders confirmed that if core demands were not addressed before the World Cup (June 11 opener at Estadio Azteca), the CNTE would escalate actions to maximize visibility during international coverage. The national strike affected schools in Oaxaca (Sección 22 ~70,000 members), Chiapas (Sección 7), Michoacán (Sección 18), Guerrero, Hidalgo, and Campeche. At her June 1 mañanera, Sheinbaum expressed confidence the dispute would be resolved via dialogue through SEP and SEGOB, dismissing concerns about World Cup disruption.

media.caption: CNTE megamarch on June 1, 2026 — tens of thousands of teachers from 29 states march through Mexico City

title: Day 608 — Sheinbaum Mañanera: Tomato Price Agreement Announced for June 3; Four Young Women to Represent Mexico at World Cup Ceremony; 18.8M Bienestar Payments June 15–21
detail: At her June 1, 2026 (Day 608) mañanera from the National Palace, President Claudia Sheinbaum announced several policy and social actions: (1) TOMATO PRICES: Sheinbaum confirmed she would sign an agreement with tomato producers and distributors on Wednesday, June 3, to address a three-month spike in tomato prices. She cited Florida frosts, crop disease in Sinaloa, and intermediary markups as causes. The government plan: direct connections between producers and central market distribution systems. (2) FIFA WORLD CUP 2026: Sheinbaum presented four young women who will represent Mexico at the FIFA World Cup 2026 inauguration ceremony at Estadio Azteca on June 11 (Mexico vs. South Africa) — selected through national competitions. Sheinbaum had previously given her personal presidential ticket (ticket #0001) to Yolett Cervantes Cuaquehua, a 21-year-old Indigenous woman from Veracruz, at the May 29 mañanera. (3) CNTE: Expressed confidence that the teachers' dispute would be resolved via dialogue through SEP Secretary Mario Delgado and Interior Secretary Rosa Icela Rodríguez, without disrupting World Cup activities. (4) WELFARE / BIENESTAR: Announced bienestar card distribution for elderly adults and registered women, scheduled June 15–21, with new registration opening June 22–28 — affecting 18.8 million beneficiaries representing 663 million pesos. (5) SOVEREIGNTY / US PRESSURE: In response to questions about U.S. pressure and the DOJ indictment campaign, Sheinbaum reiterated her sovereignty posture at the mañanera: 'We are not anyone's puppet. If from abroad culprits are dictated and pressure is sought, that is interference.' She confirmed the FGR found no basis to charge Chihuahua Governor Maru Campos, framing external pressure as 'foreign interference.'

media.caption: Sheinbaum's June 1 Day 608 mañanera — tomato price agreement, World Cup ceremony, Bienestar payments, sovereignty posture
